## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Jīvitindriyakathā* (Kv 8.10) is a debate located in the eighth chapter (*vagga*) of the *Kathāvatthu*, within the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. According to the commentary, the controversy is conducted between the Theravādin (*Sakavādin*) and interlocutors identified as the Pubbaseliyas and the Sammitīyas over whether there are two distinct life-faculties (*jīvitindriya*) or only one [Karunadasa 1967]. The Sakavādin maintains that there are two forms of the life-faculty—a physical life-faculty (*rūpa-jīvitindriya*) and a mental life-faculty (*nāma-* or *arūpa-jīvitindriya*)—arguing that this distinction is required to explain why the attainment of cessation (*nirodhasamāpatti*) does not constitute death, and why beings in the non-percipient realm (*asaññabhava*) still possess life despite lacking mental factors [Karunadasa 1967]. In contrast, the opponents contend that there is only one life-faculty, which is non-material (*arūpa*) and common to both mind and matter; as the commentary notes, they treat the life-faculty as a non-material phenomenon dissociated from mind (*citta-vippayutta-arūpa-dhamma*), closely paralleling the Sarvāstivāda-Vaibhāṣika classification of vitality among the *cittaviprayuktasamskāras* [Karunadasa 1967].
